correctness.rationale: Sparse paving rank r≥3 and corank≥3 has exactly the coordinate 2n facets plus one facet per circuit-hyperplane, by connected-flat facet conditions; the coordinate facets are active at all bases, and precisely t(B) hyperplane facets join them. The primitive normals live in N=Z^n/Z·1 and the signed coordinate rays span it saturately, giving torsion-free Cl(X)=Z^(n+h+1) and Cl(U_B)=Z^(1+t(B)). At every vertex n>n−1 rays make U_B singular and non-Q-factorial. Local rational Cartier equations require the unique sign vector a_i=1 for i∈B, −1 otherwise to descend, imposing n=2r; each active H pairs to r−2 so imposes t(B)=0 or r=3. The vector is then integral, hence rational Cartier iff Cartier, no finite nontrivial index. With h>0 some B has t>0; global criterion follows. Exhaustively recomputed Vámos 65 bases, counts t=0,1,2 of 17,16,32; 6 automorphism orbits sizes 1,16,16,8,8,16 with claimed t. These finite checks corroborate, but the universal proof rests on matroid facets and toric divisor sequences.
residual_risks: Current proof establishes singular/Q-factorial behavior at torus-fixed points and global Cartier status, not positive-dimensional singular-stratum classification or Jacobian scheme.
Toric semigroup and normal-fan Gorenstein constructions can be confused in the literature; the exact distinction must be preserved in publication.
